key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly screen multilayer perovskite solar-cell stacks and pinpoint high-efficiency, lead-free architectures by ranking ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable design strategy for optimizing interfacial materials and band alignment in perovskite solar cells without exhaustively simulating every possible stack.
method: Simulated 125 ETL/absorber/HTL device architectures with SCAPS-1D.
Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unseen configurations.
Used SHAP to identify the most influential descriptors: HTL band gap, absorber band gap, and ETL electron affinity.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed strong Spearman rank correlation, and the top ML-suggested devices were confirmed by full SCAPS-1D simulations, including 28.85% PCE for FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag.
watch_item: Performance depends on the representativeness of the simulated training set, so the ML rankings may be less reliable when extrapolating beyond the explored material/property space.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
